title: Cohere Embeddings
guide-section: Building a Store

`EmbeddingCohere` creates embeddings using [Cohere](https://cohere.com) models. You can pass it to a raghilda store or call it directly to embed text.

## Installation

Install Cohere's Python package in the same environment as raghilda:

```bash
pip install cohere
```

Get an API key from the [Cohere dashboard](https://dashboard.cohere.com/api-keys) and set the `CO_API_KEY` environment variable before creating a provider:

```bash
export CO_API_KEY="..."
```

You can also pass the key directly with `api_key=`. raghilda doesn't save API keys with the store, so set `CO_API_KEY` when [reconnecting](#reconnecting-to-a-store).

## Basic usage

Use `model=` to choose a model. These examples use `embed-v5.0-fast`, from Cohere's [Embed 5 release](https://docs.cohere.com/changelog/embed-v5) in September 2026. Calling `EmbeddingCohere()` without a model still selects `embed-english-v3.0`.

::: {#e7967d80 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingCohere

provider = EmbeddingCohere(model="embed-v5.0-fast")
```
:::


Pass the provider to a store through the `embed=` argument:

::: {#7373ae4f .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingCohere

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="my_store.db",
    embed=EmbeddingCohere(model="embed-v5.0-fast"),
)
```
:::


`DuckDBStore.create()` calls the embedding API to determine the size of the embeddings, so it needs a working API key.

## Choosing a model

These models support the text embedding API used by `EmbeddingCohere`. The list was reviewed in November 2026:

| Model                | Dimensions | Notes                                                         |
| -------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `embed-v5.0-fast`    | 2048       | Multilingual; the model used in this guide                    |
| `embed-v5.0-pro`     | 2048       | Multilingual; another v5 model to compare on your searches    |
| `embed-v4.0`         | 1536       | Previous generation; may already be used in an existing store |
| `embed-english-v3.0` | 1024       | English; raghilda's default                                   |

Dimensions are the number of values in each embedding. They affect storage size, but do not tell you which model will retrieve the most useful passages. The table shows the dimensions returned by raghilda; the provider does not expose Cohere's `output_dimension` option.

To compare models, choose a few questions for which you know the relevant passages. Build a separate store with each model, using the same documents and chunks, and check whether those passages appear in the results. Response time and API cost may also affect your choice.

Cohere's [model documentation](https://docs.cohere.com/docs/cohere-embed) lists supported languages and input limits. The v3 English model accepts up to 512 tokens per input, while v4 and v5 accept longer inputs. Check the limit when choosing a [chunk size](chunking.qmd), since text beyond it may be truncated by the API.

::: {.callout-note}
A store saves the model it was created with. To use a different model, create a new store and embed your documents again.
:::

## Query and document embeddings

Cohere's embedding API uses an input type to distinguish search queries from documents. raghilda maps `EmbedInputType.QUERY` to `"search_query"` and `EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT` to `"search_document"`. `DuckDBStore` sets the input type automatically: chunks added with `upsert()` or `ingest()` use the document type, and text passed to `retrieve()` uses the query type.

When calling the provider directly, set `input_type` to match the text you're embedding:

::: {#bf9a09c5 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingCohere, EmbedInputType

provider = EmbeddingCohere(model="embed-v5.0-fast")

# Embed documents for storage
doc_embeddings = provider.embed(
    ["Retrieval-Augmented Generation grounds LLM responses in source material."],
    input_type=EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT,
)

# Embed a query for search
query_embedding = provider.embed(
    ["What is RAG?"],
    input_type=EmbedInputType.QUERY,
)
```
:::


If you leave out `input_type`, the provider assumes `EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT`.

::: {.callout-note}
### Set the input type for search queries

Embedding a search query with the default `DOCUMENT` type can give less relevant results without raising an error. When calling `embed()` directly, pass `input_type=EmbedInputType.QUERY` for queries and `EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT` for stored documents. `DuckDBStore` sets these values for you.

Choose the type by the text's role in the search. A query such as "password reset" uses `QUERY`, even though it isn't a question. A stored help article headed "How do I reset my password?" uses `DOCUMENT`.
:::

## Batching and rate limits

Cohere accepts up to 96 texts per request. `EmbeddingCohere` uses a default `batch_size` of 96 and splits larger inputs into batches.

If Cohere responds with a rate-limit error (HTTP 429), the provider waits and retries. If the retries fail, it raises the error.

## Reconnecting to a store

The store saves the model name and batch size. `DuckDBStore.connect()` uses these settings to restore the provider:

::: {#d5b6d9cb .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

store = DuckDBStore.connect("my_store.db")
chunks = store.retrieve("What is RAG?", top_k=5)
```
:::


Set `CO_API_KEY` in the session that reconnects to the store, since the saved configuration doesn't include the API key.

## Parameters

All parameters are optional when `CO_API_KEY` is set:

| Parameter    | Default                | Description                                                  |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `model`      | `"embed-english-v3.0"` | Cohere embedding model name                                  |
| `api_key`    | `None`                 | API key. Falls back to the `CO_API_KEY` environment variable |
| `batch_size` | `96`                   | Texts per API call. Cohere allows at most 96                 |

See the [`EmbeddingCohere` reference page](/reference/embedding.EmbeddingCohere.qmd) for API details.

## Complete example

This example creates a store, adds web pages, builds search indexes, and runs a query. Replace the example URLs with pages you want to search.

::: {#c54c2547 .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingCohere
from raghilda.read import read_as_markdown
from raghilda.chunker import MarkdownChunker

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="docs.db",
    embed=EmbeddingCohere(model="embed-v5.0-fast"),
    name="docs",
    title="My Documentation",
    overwrite=True,
)

chunker = MarkdownChunker()
for url in ["https://example.com/doc1", "https://example.com/doc2"]:
    store.upsert(chunker.chunk(read_as_markdown(url)))

store.build_index()

chunks = store.retrieve("How does authentication work?", top_k=5)
for chunk in chunks:
    print(chunk.text[:200])
```
:::


Each page is converted to Markdown, split into chunks, and embedded as documents. `build_index()` builds the vector and keyword indexes, and `retrieve()` embeds the question as a query before searching.

## Using Cohere with ChromaDB

ChromaDB 1.5.9's [Cohere embedding function](https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma/blob/11f3c7435e71024aa0a2b53710a28d3289d922d1/chromadb/utils/embedding_functions/cohere_embedding_function.py#L73-L80) uses `search_document` for queries as well as stored text. Use `DuckDBStore` for the query/document behavior described above.

When you pass `EmbeddingCohere` to `ChromaDBStore`, raghilda converts it to ChromaDB's `CohereEmbeddingFunction`. ChromaDB saves the configuration and restores it when you reconnect:

::: {#072d96c0 .cell execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from raghilda.store import ChromaDBStore
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingCohere

store = ChromaDBStore.create(
    location="chroma_store",
    embed=EmbeddingCohere(model="embed-v5.0-fast"),
    name="documents",
)

# Later, reconnect without specifying `embed=`
store = ChromaDBStore.connect(name="documents", location="chroma_store")
```
:::


See [ChromaDB Embedding Functions](chromadb-embedding-functions.qmd) for details on reconnecting and supplying API keys.
